# @ternent/identity

> One Ed25519 identity: create, back up, restore, recover from words, sign and verify.

All exports come from the package root. Declarations: `dist/index.d.ts`.
[Public README](https://github.com/ternent/core/blob/main/packages/identity/README.md).

```ts
import {
  createIdentity,
  restoreIdentity,
  createMnemonicIdentity,
  recoverIdentity,
  verify,
  validatePublicIdentity,
  type Identity,
  type PublicIdentity,
} from "@ternent/identity";

const identity = await createIdentity();
const backup = identity.export(); // JSON with the private seed; the app stores it
const restored = await restoreIdentity(backup);
const signature = await identity.sign(bytes); // 64 bytes over exactly `bytes`
const ok = await verify(identity.publicIdentity, bytes, signature);
```

- Pass the `Identity` itself to Ledger, Seal and Armour. Do not decode the seed or
  build a second signer.
- `PublicIdentity` is `{ version: 1, algorithm: "Ed25519", publicKey, id }` with a
  base64url key and `id = "identity:" + hex(sha256(publicKey))`. It is safe to put
  in documents. Check untrusted values with `validatePublicIdentity` (throws).
- `verify` never throws; it returns `false` for a bad identity, signature or match.
- `restoreIdentity`, `recoverIdentity` and `createMnemonicIdentity` reject with an
  ordinary `Error` on invalid input.
- `withX25519Secret(use)` lends a temporary X25519 secret for decryption and zeroes
  it after `use` settles. Do not retain it.
- Recovery words are opt-in, shown once, and never part of the backup.
- Encryption, storage, accounts and two-factor checks belong to the application.
